segments.en: These two letters, written from Uman — the resting place of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov — introduce us to Rabbi Shimshon Barski as a deeply devoted Breslov Chassid, serving as a spiritual mentor and guide to a circle of Anash based in Lublin.

Letter 1 (5669 — Eve of Shavuos): Written in a mixture of Hebrew and Yiddish, this brief but piercing letter responds to a quarrel (machlokes) that has erupted in the Lublin shtibel. Rabbi Shimshon delivers a powerful rebuke through an agricultural metaphor rooted in Rebbe Nachman's teachings: just as a kernel of grain must first rot in the earth, then endure reaping, threshing, grinding, kneading, and baking before it can nourish a human being — so too, anyone who wishes to draw close to the Rebbe's inner light must pass through birurim (refinements), trials, humiliations, and tests. The sting of the rebuke is sharp: the community has not yet endured a single real trial, yet they already wish to settle comfortably in worldly honor and build their own shtibels.
